summary: The wake gate proves it can still wake at startup, and says so in one greppable line — a gate that cannot wake no longer looks identical to one nobody has spoken to.
details: At boot the service drives a known 「喂 Nora」 clip through the PRODUCTION path — the sidecar's 20ms 48kHz stereo frame shape, the stereo fold, the 3:1 downsample, the real ONNX model and the real gate — and logs `wake selftest: PASS|FAIL|ERROR` with the peak score. The clip is tracked in git beside the model for the same reason the model is.

The three outcomes stay distinct and fail closed. PASS means a known clip woke the gate; FAIL means the audio was scored and did not wake it; ERROR means the path could not be exercised at all. ERROR is never PASS, and FAIL and ERROR point at opposite causes.

A `wake summary` line every five minutes carries gates, clients, frames, chunks, wakes, utterances and the self-test verdict, so `grep 'wake summary'` answers "is this feature dead?" without correlating anything: arms climbing while wakes stay at zero IS the failure.
/health now carries the self-test verdict, so monitoring can assert the property rather than the process being up.

Neither check can stop the service. A gate that cannot self-test still serves, and the operator's signal is the log line, not a crash loop that would destroy the evidence — the same posture as the existing liveness-not-readiness /health.
limitations: This detects the failure at startup and reports it continuously; it does not explain the 2026-09-18 occurrence, whose cause was not recoverable from what survived.
A model that passes at boot and degrades later is caught by the per-window peak logging, not by the self-test, which runs once.
